title: Kinetic and thermodynamic analysis of tar‐rich coal pyrolysis: Comparison between model‐free and model‐fitting methods
content:
Abstract

The pyrolysis of tar-rich coal plays a critical role in the efficient utilization of energy and the production of chemicals. This study presents a comprehensive kinetic and thermodynamic analysis of Xinjiang tar-rich coal pyrolysis, employing both model-free and model-fitting approaches. The results reveal that the dominant pyrolysis mechanism transitions with temperature, and the activation energy reaches its minimum at α = 0.4, highlighting the multi-step nature of the process. The model-free method provides higher activation energy values, offering a more accurate depiction of the intrinsic kinetics. Thermodynamic analysis indicates that the pyrolysis reaction is endothermic (ΔH > 230 kJ/mol), with a significant rise in enthalpy to 298.80 kJ/mol at higher temperatures (α = 0.7), likely due to intense depolymerization of coal's molecular structure. ΔS is consistently negative (−283.26 to −266.19 J/(mol·K)) and decreases in magnitude with increasing conversion, reflecting a reduction in system disorder, likely due to graphitization and volatile loss. ΔG remains positive (427–488 kJ/mol), confirming that the reaction is non-spontaneous and requires continuous external heating. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing tar yield and optimizing operational conditions in both industrial and in-situ pyrolysis processes.
